targets.role: Canonical implementation; the public list-refusals.mjs compatibility facade re-exports this module.

preserve: listSay substitutes data words and carries a detail code and named values
List refusal outcomes do not imply an undispatched command
allowed_deltas: The active target omits the original ConfigurationError import and its special refusal branch; its list-specific refusal and word substitution mechanisms remain.
A fresh canonical core contains the adapted behavior; the existing public module path is a thin re-export facade and adds no historical-copy claim.
banned_substitutions: Using the archived source to claim active line retention
Claiming the original active module was copied before adaptation

baseline.scope: The immutable original source copy at baseline.path is recovery evidence only. The active core is introduced after this NEW baseline, and the pre-existing public module path is rewritten as a thin compatibility facade after it. This does not claim the original migration was source-first or that the facade was historically copied first.

active_retention.method: Independently compare source lines trimmed and length >=24 against only the active target's trimmed lines; archive excluded. The general validator's combined-target retention is not this active measurement.

proof.privacy_and_rights: The owner authorized recovery of their repository-owned code. Historical source contains generic refusal code, relative module comments and no credentials, personal identifiers or customer content; no LICENSE file existed at the inspected source commit. Source identity uses a private path hash; archive is evidence only.

active_target.method: Trim each source and active-core line; keep lines of length >=24; count source lines present in the core line set. The immutable archive and compatibility facade are excluded.
